## Statistical Deep Dive

The Rays came in with a 61% win probability—a solid edge, but not overwhelming. When you're looking at probabilities in the 60-65% range, you're essentially saying the model sees a clear advantage but acknowledges variance. That 61% translated to a win, which is exactly what we expect over a large sample size.

A single game doesn't validate a model, but it does validate the process. The data pointed to Tampa Bay, and Tampa Bay delivered.

## What the 100% Really Means

Look, I'm a numbers guy, so let me be clear: a 100% win rate on one game is statistically interesting but not predictive of future performance. What matters is that we're following the model, trusting the probabilities, and letting the law of large numbers work in our favor.

The real metric to watch? Long-term accuracy trends. One perfect day is great, but it's the cumulative win rate over dozens and hundreds of games that tells the real story.
